To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: READ BEFORE YOUR NEXT COLOUR: Brightline Pro 6% developer, batch LX2291 may be 12%

Please read this before your next colour client.

Kelvin Trade have emailed to say there was a filling error on one batch of Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L. Batch LX2291 may actually contain 12% (40 vol), whatever the label says. They say it was supplied between 19 October and 5 November, and that other batches and strengths are fine. Plenty of us buy from the same rep, so it's worth checking even if you think you're clear.

Why I'm putting this up: on Saturday I used a bottle from this batch and a client's scalp was burnt. Aileen had it on Thursday too. Her highlights client lifted far too fast and the foils were roasting, and she thought she'd left the heater too close. Kelvin Trade's email says sorry for any inconvenience. It's not an inconvenience, it's a burnt scalp.

HOW TO CHECK
- Turn the bottle over. The batch code is printed on the BASE of the bottle. The box doesn't have it, so don't check the box.
- You're looking for LX2291.
- Check the open bottles in your trolley as well as the stock in the back.
- If you bought any developer from the rep between 19 Oct and 5 Nov, check it. Lorna, I think you got a box off him too.

IF YOU HAVE IT
- Stop using it and put it somewhere separate so nobody grabs it by mistake.
- The rep is in on Tuesday and you can hand bottles back to him. You can also take them to the Kelvin Trade depot in Hillington. Either way it's a full credit.
- If you've had a problem with a client, KEEP THAT BOTTLE. Don't bin it. Hand back the others but hold on to that one.
- Take a photo of the base showing the batch code, and write down what happened while you still remember it: what you mixed, timings, what the client said and when. It's also worth letting your own insurer know.

WHAT IT DOES
It's double the strength you think you're using. Expect much faster lift, more heat, and a real chance of burning the scalp. On Saturday, a retouch that normally takes 35-40 minutes was near pale yellow at 18, and the client went from a normal tingle at 10 minutes to burning at the crown by 18. Things to look out for:
- A client saying it's burning or stinging earlier than usual, or more than usual
- Foils or the head feeling hot
- Lift going way faster than normal
- Patchy, brassy or over-processed hair afterwards
- Redness on the scalp or nape

It applies to anything you mixed with it, so that includes toners and tints as well as bleach and highlights. The liquid looks and feels the same as normal, so you won't be able to tell by looking.

If you've done anyone since 19 Oct with a bottle from this batch and they've been sore or had odd results, it's worth getting in touch with them.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR
- Rinse straight away with cool running water. No shampoo. Wear gloves yourself.
- Keep rinsing, and don't put any creams or anything else on it. The NHS advice for chemical burns is to rinse for about an hour, and they need looking at in hospital.
- Get someone to phone 999 and follow what the call handler says. Don't wait for blistering or for it to get worse.
- If there's any trouble breathing, swelling of the throat or face, or the client collapses, that's 999 immediately.
- Once the client is sorted, write it in the incident book at the desk, and keep the bottle.

Gail's patch test and first aid notes are in How We Do Things if you want to look back over them. A patch test won't catch this, though, because it's the strength of the developer that's wrong and not an allergy.

If you're not sure about a bottle, don't use it. Ask me or Aileen and we'll look at it with you.

Kirsty
